                "uuid": "019fb87c-83de-7a70-90c5-a833b0cbc40a",
                "text": "Yes, this makes complete sense and it's actually the **right** UX decision. Here's why:\n\n**Homepage = Brand/Trust moment.** When a user lands, they should feel like they're dealing with something legitimate and serious \u2014 not immediately bombarded with permission popups. A clean, minimal homepage builds that trust first.\n\n**Consent screen = Separate, intentional step.** By navigating to a dedicated consent page, the user is making a conscious decision to proceed. This also has a legal advantage \u2014 it creates a clear, isolated consent moment which is important for KYC specifically. If consent and the action are on the same page, it feels rushed and looks unprofessional.\n\nSo your flow makes sense:\n\n```\nHomepage (clean, minimal, one CTA button)\n    \u2193\nConsent Screen (clearly lists what will be accessed \u2014 camera, mic, location \u2014 user agrees)\n    \u2193\nKYC Session (WebRTC starts only AFTER consent)\n```\n\nThis is actually how banks and financial institutions structure their KYC flows too \u2014 consent is always a separate, deliberate screen.\n\nWhat's your next doubt?",

                "uuid": "019fb87d-cff3-70fd-b615-00364c95ba89",
                "text": "Yes, makes sense for a prototype \u2014 skip the consent page, just get straight to testing the functionality.\n\nBut one practical heads-up: **browsers don't ask for all three permissions at once.** Chrome requests them one at a time, and also \u2014 **location permission is separate from camera/mic.** So the flow will naturally be:\n\n```\nUser opens homepage\n    \u2193\nChrome asks \u2192 Allow Camera & Microphone?  [Allow]\n    \u2193\nChrome asks \u2192 Allow Location?  [Allow]\n    \u2193\nSession starts automatically \u2192 streams to admin\n```\n\nAlso one important thing \u2014 **WebRTC with camera/mic only works on HTTPS or localhost.** Since you're testing on your smartphone, your phone and PC need to be either:\n\n- On the **same WiFi network** (local IP works), or\n- Deployed on **HTTPS** (even a free Vercel deployment works)\n\nOtherwise Chrome on mobile will block the camera/mic access entirely \u2014 not an AI Studio limitation, it's a browser security rule.\n\nSo just to confirm the prototype flow before you move on:\n\n- User opens the page \u2192 permissions auto-requested \u2192 stream starts \u2192 admin sees it live\n- Admin is on a **separate URL/page** that you open on your PC/another device\n- No login for prototype, just two direct URLs \u2014 one for user, one for admin?\n\nOr do you still want even a basic hardcoded login?",
                "content": [

                "text": "Yes, JWT works perfectly for this. And good thinking on hosting early \u2014 **Vercel** is the obvious choice here since you're on Next.js. Free tier, instant deployment, automatic HTTPS, and your phone will work with it out of the box. No configuration needed.\n\nSo the final prototype flow is clean:\n\n```\nUser Side (no auth)\nHomepage opens \u2192 Chrome requests camera + mic + location \u2192 stream starts \u2192 waiting for admin\n\nAdmin Side (JWT auth)\n/admin/login \u2192 hardcoded credentials \u2192 JWT issued \u2192 /admin/dashboard \u2192 sees live feed + location + approve/reject\n```\n\nOne thing worth clarifying though \u2014 JWT for admin works fine, but since this is Next.js you have two options for where the token lives:\n\n- **httpOnly cookie** \u2014 more secure, token never touches JavaScript, better practice\n- **localStorage** \u2014 simpler to implement but less secure\n\nFor a prototype that you're also considering hosting, I'd say go with **httpOnly cookie** from the start. It's not much extra work and you won't have to redo it later when you go production.\n\nDoes that work for you? And one more thing \u2014 for the admin dashboard, do you want the live user sessions to appear automatically when a user connects, or should the admin manually refresh/check?",

                "uuid": "019fb8a0-fd45-76b8-aa12-84e3cffcafce",
                "text": "Yes, this is absolutely possible and it's a brilliant solution actually. Very practical for a solo admin setup. Let me confirm the full flow:\n\n**Admin Offline Flow:**\n```\nUser connects \u2192 socket detects admin is offline\n\u2192 Socket sends browser notification to admin \n  (Chrome push notification \u2014 even if tab is in background)\n\u2192 User sees a minimal \"Please wait, connecting you to admin...\"\n  with a subtle 120 second countdown (not too obvious, just a small indicator)\n```\n\n**Two outcomes after 120 seconds:**\n\n```\nOutcome 1 \u2014 Admin comes online within 120s:\n\u2192 Countdown disappears silently\n\u2192 Session starts normally as if nothing happened\n\u2192 User never knew there was an issue\n\nOutcome 2 \u2014 Admin doesn't come online in 120s:\n\u2192 User sees:\n  \"Admin is currently unavailable\"\n  \"Would you like to record a message instead?\"\n\u2192 User clicks record\n\u2192 Camera/mic already active (permissions already granted)\n\u2192 User records video of themselves + documents (no time limit)\n\u2192 Submits \u2192 stored in MongoDB\n\u2192 User sees \"Your message has been sent, \n   admin will review it shortly\"\n\u2192 Admin gets notification of recorded message when they come online\n```\n\n**Tech behind it:**\n```\nChrome Push Notifications \u2192 Web Push API + service worker\n120s countdown \u2192 simple server side socket timer\nVideo recording \u2192 MediaRecorder API \n  (camera/mic already active so no extra permissions needed)\nRecorded video storage \u2192 MongoDB GridFS \n  (handles large video files in chunks)\n```\n\nThis is completely possible and honestly very well thought out. The fact that camera/mic permissions are already granted by the time the 120s kicks in makes the recording flow seamless \u2014 no extra steps for the user at all.\n\nDoes this match what you had in mind?",

                "uuid": "019fb8a7-f2d6-7a73-b78b-bda5320ea2c8",
                "text": "Perfect, all noted. Now let me explain the STUN server in simple terms:\n\n---\n\n### What is a STUN Server?\n\nThink of it this way \u2014\n\nYour phone and your PC are both connected to the same WiFi, but they don't know each other's **exact network address** to send video directly to each other. They know their **local IP** (like 192.168.1.5) but WebRTC needs to figure out the **best path** to send data between two devices.\n\nA STUN server is basically a **middleman that just answers one question:**\n\n> \"Hey, what does my connection look like from the outside world?\"\n\n```\nYour Phone \u2192 asks STUN server \u2192 \"what's my public address?\"\nSTUN server \u2192 replies \u2192 \"you look like X.X.X.X to the outside\"\nPhone shares that info with PC via Socket.io\nPC does the same\nNow they know how to reach each other directly\nSTUN server's job is done \u2014 it leaves the conversation\n```\n\n**Important:** STUN server does NOT carry your video. It only helps devices **find each other**. After that the video flows directly phone \u2194 PC (peer to peer).\n\n**For your prototype** \u2014 Google provides a free STUN server:\n```\nstun:stun.l.google.com:19302\n```\nThis one line in the WebRTC config is all you need. No setup, no cost, just works.\n\n---\n\n### When would STUN fail?\n\nOnly if you're on a very strict corporate/university network that blocks peer connections. Your home WiFi \u2014 it'll work perfectly.\n\n---\n\nNow all points are addressed. Summary of decisions made:\n\n```\nUser identity \u2192 skip for prototype\nMultiple users \u2192 admin identifies by feed visually\nSTUN server \u2192 Google's free STUN server\nUser disconnects \u2192 show \"User disconnected\" on admin grid\nAdmin disconnects \u2192 show \"Admin disconnected\" on user screen\nRecorded video \u2192 120 seconds max\n               \u2192 compressed for storage (minimal size)\n               \u2192 decompressed to original quality on playback\nChat file size \u2192 no limit for admin\nSnapshot \u2192 stored in MongoDB as compressed image\n         \u2192 used only for cross-verification disputes\n```\n\nAre we good to move forward or anything else to discuss?",

                "uuid": "019fb8a9-a5bb-7dde-804a-f5298423e34f",
                "text": "Great question and you're absolutely right to flag this. Let me explain clearly:\n\n---\n\n### The Reality of AI Studio Hosting\n\nWhen AI Studio runs your app it's on **Google's servers**, not your PC. So the network situation becomes:\n\n```\nYour Phone \u2192 Google's Server (AI Studio) \u2192 Your PC (admin browser)\n```\n\nThis means it's **no longer same WiFi** \u2014 it's going through the public internet. So STUN alone **won't be enough**.\n\n---\n\n### STUN vs TURN \u2014 The Difference\n\n```\nSTUN \u2192 just helps devices find each other's address\n      \u2192 works when devices can connect directly\n      \u2192 FREE\n\nTURN \u2192 when direct connection fails, TURN server \n      acts as a relay \u2014 video actually passes through it\n      \u2192 needed when behind different networks/firewalls\n      \u2192 usually COSTS money (bandwidth)\n```\n\nFor AI Studio's `*.ai.studio` domain \u2014 since admin and user are on completely different networks (one is your phone, one is your PC, both going through Google's server) \u2014 **you'll need a TURN server** as fallback.\n\n---\n\n### Free Solution for Prototype\n\n**Metered.ca** offers a free TURN server for prototypes:\n```\nFree tier \u2192 50GB bandwidth/month\n\u2192 More than enough for testing\n\u2192 No credit card needed\n\u2192 Takes 2 minutes to set up\n```\n\nOr **Cloudflare TURN** \u2014 also free for low usage.\n\n---\n\n### So your WebRTC config will look like:\n\n```\nICE Servers configuration:\n1. Google STUN (primary \u2014 tries direct connection first)\n2. Metered TURN (fallback \u2014 if direct fails, relays through server)\n```\n\nThis combination means:\n```\nSame WiFi \u2192 STUN handles it (direct, fast)\nDifferent networks / AI Studio hosting \u2192 TURN kicks in (relayed)\nBoth cases \u2192 WebRTC works perfectly\n```\n\n---\n\n### Bottom Line\n\n```\nLocal testing (same WiFi) \u2192 STUN only \u2192 works\nAI Studio *.ai.studio hosting \u2192 STUN + TURN \u2192 works\nVercel deployment (later) \u2192 STUN + TURN \u2192 works\n```\n\nSo yes \u2014 for AI Studio hosting you need TURN configured. But it's free, quick to set up, and I'll include it in the prompt when you're ready. You'll just need to create a free account on Metered.ca and get the credentials.\n\nDoes this make sense?",

                "text": "\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nGood \u2014 straight from the official Google AI documentation, last updated yesterday (July 30, 2026). Here's the full honest breakdown:\n\n---\n\n## Available Models in Google AI Studio (Official, Current)\n\n### Gemini 3 Family\n| Model | Status | Best For |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Gemini 3.6 Flash** | \u2705 Stable | Speed + intelligence, agentic tasks |\n| **Gemini 3.5 Flash** | \u2705 Stable | Frontier performance, coding, agents |\n| **Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite** | \u2705 Stable | Fast, cost-effective, high throughput |\n| **Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite** | \u2705 Stable | Budget, lightweight tasks |\n| **Gemini 3.1 Pro** | \u26a0\ufe0f Preview | Complex reasoning, vibe coding |\n\n### Gemini 2.5 Family\n| Model | Status | Best For |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Gemini 2.5 Pro** | \u2705 Stable | Deep reasoning, complex tasks |\n| **Gemini 2.5 Flash** | \u2705 Stable | Price-performance, reasoning |\n| **Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite** | \u2705 Stable | Fastest, budget-friendly |\n\n---\n\n## Which One for YOUR Project?\n\nGiven your priorities are **security-sensitive code + complex WebRTC architecture + full stack Next.js**, here's the honest recommendation:\n\n### \u2705 Use: **Gemini 2.5 Pro (Stable)**\n\nHere's why over everything else:\n\n**Why not Gemini 3.1 Pro?** \u2014 It's still **Preview** status. Preview means it can be deprecated with just 2 weeks notice, more restrictive rate limits, and behaviour can change unexpectedly. For a security-focused project you don't want your model changing mid-build.\n\n**Why not Gemini 3.5 Flash or 3.6 Flash?** \u2014 Flash models are optimised for speed and throughput. Your project needs **deep reasoning** \u2014 WebRTC signalling logic, JWT security patterns, Socket.io architecture, MongoDB GridFS \u2014 Flash models cut corners on architectural complexity.\n\n**Why Gemini 2.5 Pro Stable?** \u2014\n- Most advanced model for complex tasks, featuring deep reasoning and coding capabilities\n- **Stable** \u2014 won't change or get deprecated unexpectedly mid-build\n- Battle-tested, predictable, well-documented behaviour\n- Best for security-critical code generation where correctness matters more than speed\n- Gemini 2.5 Pro at $2/1M input tokens is roughly on par with Claude Sonnet 4 \u2014 strong intelligence per dollar\n\n**Set Thinking to: High** \u2014 this makes 2.5 Pro reason deeply before generating, which is critical for your WebRTC + security architecture.\n\n---\n\nSo in AI Studio Build mode: **Model \u2192 Gemini 2.5 Pro, Thinking \u2192 High.** That's your setup.",

patterns\n\nGemini models are available in either *stable*, *preview*, *latest*, or *experimental* versions.\n\n**Note:** The following list refers to the model string naming convention as of\nSeptember, 2025. Models released prior to that may have different naming\nconventions. Refer to the exact model string if you are using an older model.\n\n### Stable\n\nPoints to a specific stable model. Stable models usually don't change. Most\nproduction apps should use a specific stable model.\n\nFor example: `gemini-3.6-flash`.\n\n### Preview\n\nPoints to a preview model which may be used for production. Preview models will\ntypically have billing enabled, might come with more restrictive rate limits and\nwill be deprecated with at least 2 weeks notice.\n\nFor example: `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-09-2025`.\n\n### Latest\n\nPoints to the latest release for a specific model variation. This can be a\nstable, preview or experimental release. This alias will get hot-swapped with\nevery new release of a specific model variation. For breaking changes, a **2-week notice** will be provided through email before the version behind\nlatest is changed.\n\nFor example: `gemini-flash-latest`.\n\n### Experimental\n\nPoints to an experimental model which will typically be not be suitable for\nproduction use and come with more restrictive rate limits. We release\nexperimental models to gather feedback and get our latest updates into the hands\nof developers quickly.\n\nExperimental models are not stable and availability of model endpoints is\nsubject to change.\n\n## Model deprecations\n\nFor information about model deprecations, visit the [Gemini deprecations](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations) page.\n\nSend feedback\n\nExcept as otherwise noted, the content of this page is licensed under the [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 License](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), and code samples are licensed under the [Apache 2.0 License](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0).                         "text": "Good \u2014 straight from the official Google AI documentation, last updated yesterday (July 30, 2026). Here's the full honest breakdown:\n\n---\n\n## Available Models in Google AI Studio (Official, Current)\n\n### Gemini 3 Family\n| Model | Status | Best For |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Gemini 3.6 Flash** | \u2705 Stable | Speed + intelligence, agentic tasks |\n| **Gemini 3.5 Flash** | \u2705 Stable | Frontier performance, coding, agents |\n| **Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite** | \u2705 Stable | Fast, cost-effective, high throughput |\n| **Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite** | \u2705 Stable | Budget, lightweight tasks |\n| **Gemini 3.1 Pro** | \u26a0\ufe0f Preview | Complex reasoning, vibe coding |\n\n### Gemini 2.5 Family\n| Model | Status | Best For |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Gemini 2.5 Pro** | \u2705 Stable | Deep reasoning, complex tasks |\n| **Gemini 2.5 Flash** | \u2705 Stable | Price-performance, reasoning |\n| **Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite** | \u2705 Stable | Fastest, budget-friendly |\n\n---\n\n## Which One for YOUR Project?\n\nGiven your priorities are **security-sensitive code + complex WebRTC architecture + full stack Next.js**, here's the honest recommendation:\n\n### \u2705 Use: **Gemini 2.5 Pro (Stable)**\n\nHere's why over everything else:\n\n**Why not Gemini 3.1 Pro?** \u2014 It's still **Preview** status. Preview means it can be deprecated with just 2 weeks notice, more restrictive rate limits, and behaviour can change unexpectedly. For a security-focused project you don't want your model changing mid-build.\n\n**Why not Gemini 3.5 Flash or 3.6 Flash?** \u2014 Flash models are optimised for speed and throughput. Your project needs **deep reasoning** \u2014 WebRTC signalling logic, JWT security patterns, Socket.io architecture, MongoDB GridFS \u2014 Flash models cut corners on architectural complexity.\n\n**Why Gemini 2.5 Pro Stable?** \u2014\n- Most advanced model for complex tasks, featuring deep reasoning and coding capabilities\n- **Stable** \u2014 won't change or get deprecated unexpectedly mid-build\n- Battle-tested, predictable, well-documented behaviour\n- Best for security-critical code generation where correctness matters more than speed\n- Gemini 2.5 Pro at $2/1M input tokens is roughly on par with Claude Sonnet 4 \u2014 strong intelligence per dollar\n\n**Set Thinking to: High** \u2014 this makes 2.5 Pro reason deeply before generating, which is critical for your WebRTC + security architecture.\n\n---\n\nSo in AI Studio Build mode: **Model \u2192 Gemini 2.5 Pro, Thinking \u2192 High.** That's your setup.",

                "text": "\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nHere are 4 distinct UI concepts for your admin dashboard \u2014 pick the one that feels right and we'll lock it in before writing the prompt.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n**Option 1 \u2014 Icon sidebar + live grid.** Minimal icon-only left nav, stat cards at top, session grid below.                             {
                                "type": "text",
                                "text": "# Imagine \u2014 Visual Creation Suite\n\n## Modules\nCall read_me again with the modules parameter to load detailed guidance:\n- `diagram` \u2014 SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams\n- `mockup` \u2014 UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards\n- `interactive` \u2014 interactive explainers with controls\n- `chart` \u2014 charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3 choropleth)\n- `art` \u2014 illustration and generative art\nPick the closest fit. The module includes all relevant design guidance.\n\n**Complexity budget \u2014 hard limits:**\n- Box subtitles: \u22645 words. Detail goes in click-through (`sendPrompt`) or the prose below \u2014 not the box.\n- Colors: \u22642 ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning (states, tiers), add a 1-line legend. Otherwise use one neutral ramp.\n- Horizontal tier: \u22644 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes \u2192 shrink to \u2264110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail diagrams.\n\nIf you catch yourself writing \"click to learn more\" in prose, the diagram itself must ACTUALLY be sparse. Don't promise brevity then front-load everything.\n\n**Accessibility:** For HTML widgets, begin with a visually-hidden `<h2 class=\"sr-only\">` containing a one-sentence summary of the visualization for screen-reader users. (SVG widgets use `role=\"img\"` with `<title>` and `<desc>` instead \u2014 see SVG setup.)\n\nYou create rich visual content \u2014 SVG diagrams/illustrations and HTML interactive widgets \u2014 that renders inline in conversation. The best output feels like a natural extension of the chat.\n\n## Core Design System\n\nThese rules apply to ALL use cases.\n\n### Philosophy\n- **Seamless**: Users shouldn't notice where claude.ai ends and your widget begins.\n- **Flat**: No gradients, mesh backgrounds, noise textures, or decorative effects. Clean flat surfaces.\n- **Compact**: Show the essential inline. Explain the rest in text.\n- **Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool** \u2014 All explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element (diagram, chart, interactive widget). Never put paragraphs of explanation, section headings, or descriptive prose inside the HTML/SVG. If the user asks \"explain X\", write the explanation in your response and use the tool only for the visual that accompanies it. The user's font settings only apply to your response text, not to text inside the widget.\n\n### Streaming\nOutput streams token-by-token. Structure code so useful content appears early.\n- **HTML**: `<style>` (short) \u2192 content HTML \u2192 `<script>` last.\n- **SVG**: `<defs>` (markers) \u2192 visual elements immediately.\n- Prefer inline `style=\"...\"` over `<style>` blocks \u2014 inputs/controls must look correct mid-stream.\n- Keep `<style>` under ~15 lines. Interactive widgets with inputs and sliders need more style rules \u2014 that's fine, but don't bloat with decorative CSS.\n- Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills instead.\n\n### Rules\n- No `<!-- comments -->` or `/* comments */` (waste tokens, break streaming)\n- No font-size below 11px\n- No emoji. Icons = Tabler **outline** webfont (5800+, already loaded): `<i class=\"ti ti-home\"></i>`. Outline only \u2014 never use `-filled` suffixes (`ti-heart-filled` etc. are not loaded and will render blank). Inherits color + font-size from parent. Decorative icons get `aria-hidden=\"true\"`; icon-only buttons get `aria-label`. Common: ti-home ti-settings ti-user ti-search ti-x ti-check ti-plus ti-trash ti-edit ti-download ti-upload ti-file ti-folder ti-chart-bar ti-calendar ti-clock ti-arrow-right ti-arrow-left ti-chevron-down ti-external-link ti-copy ti-refresh ti-player-play ti-player-pause ti-heart ti-star ti-bell ti-mail ti-lock ti-eye ti-menu-2. Don't hand-draw icon SVG paths.\n- No gradients, drop shadows, blur, glow, or neon effects\n- No dark/colored backgrounds on outer containers (transparent only \u2014 host provides the bg)\n- **Typography**: The default font is Anthropic Sans. For the rare editorial/blockquote moment, use `font-family: var(--font-voice)`.\n- **Headings**: h1 = 22px, h2 = 18px, h3 = 16px \u2014 all `font-weight: 500`. Heading color is pre-set to `var(--text-primary)` \u2014 don't override it. Body text = 16px, weight 400, `line-height: 1.7`. **Two weights only: 400 regular, 500 bold.** Never use 600 or 700 \u2014 they look heavy against the host UI.\n- **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS. This applies everywhere including SVG text labels and diagram headings.\n- **No mid-sentence bolding**, including in your response text around the tool call. Entity names, class names, function names go in `code style` not **bold**. Bold is for headings and labels only.\n- The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. Your HTML fills it naturally \u2014 no wrapper div needed. Just start with your content directly. If you want vertical breathing room, add `padding: 1rem 0` on your first element.\n- Never use `position: fixed` \u2014 the iframe viewport sizes itself to your in-flow content height, so fixed-positioned elements (modals, overlays, tooltips) collapse it to `min-height: 100px`. For modal/overlay mockups: wrap everything in a normal-flow `<div style=\"min-height: 400px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.45); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;\">` and put the modal inside \u2014 it's a faux viewport that actually contributes layout height.\n- No DOCTYPE, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` \u2014 just content fragments.\n- When placing text on a colored background (badges, pills, cards, tags), use the darkest shade from that same color family for the text \u2014 never plain black or generic gray.\n- **Corners**: use `border-radius: var(--radius)` for controls, `12px` for cards. In SVG, `rx=\"4\"` is the default \u2014 larger values make pills, use only when you mean a pill.\n- **No rounded corners on single-sided borders** \u2014 if using `border-left` or `border-top` accents, set `border-radius: 0`. Rounded corners only work with full borders on all sides.\n- **No titles or prose inside the tool output** \u2014 see Philosophy above.\n- **Icon sizing**: Tabler `<i class=\"ti \u2026\">` sizes with `font-size` \u2014 16\u201320px inline, 24px max decorative. For one-off inline SVG icons, set `width`/`height` explicitly (same limits).\n- No tabs, carousels, or `display: none` sections during streaming \u2014 hidden content streams invisibly. Show all content stacked vertically. (Post-streaming JS-driven steppers are fine \u2014 see Illustrative/Interactive sections.)\n- No nested scrolling \u2014 auto-fit height.\n- Scripts execute after streaming \u2014 load libraries via `<script src=\"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...\">` (UMD globals), then use the global in a plain `<script>` that follows. The library `<script src>` tag must come BEFORE any inline script that uses its global \u2014 never call a library from code that appears above its `<script src>` tag.\n- **CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: external resources may ONLY load from `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com`, `fonts.googleapis.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`. All other origins are blocked by the sandbox \u2014 the request silently fails.\n\n### CSS Variables\n**Surfaces**: `--surface-2` (white), `--surface-1` (card), `--surface-0` (page bg); role tints `--bg-{accent,danger,success,warning}`\n**Text**: `--text-primary` (black), `--text-secondary` (muted), `--text-muted` (hints); role `--text-{accent,danger,success,warning}`\n**Borders**: `--border` (default hairline), `--border-strong` (hover), `--border-stronger`; role `--border-{accent,danger,success,warning}`\n**Typography**: `--font-sans`, `--font-voice` (serif), `--font-mono`\n**Layout**: `--radius` (8px), `--pad-{sm,md,lg,xl}`, `--gap-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}`; for larger corners use literal `12px`/`16px`\nAll auto-adapt to light/dark mode. For custom colors in HTML, use CSS variables.\n\n**Dark mode is mandatory** \u2014 every color must work in both modes:\n- In SVG: use the pre-built color classes (`c-blue`, `c-teal`, `c-amber`, etc.) for colored nodes \u2014 they handle light/dark mode automatically. Never write `<style>` blocks for colors.\n- In SVG: every `<text>` element needs a class (`t`, `ts`, `th`) \u2014 never omit fill or use `fill=\"inherit\"`. Inside a `c-{color}` parent, text classes auto-adjust to the ramp.\n- In HTML: always use CSS variables (--text-primary, --text-secondary) for text. Never hardcode colors like color: #333 \u2014 invisible in dark mode.\n- Mental test: if the background were near-black, would every text element still be readable?\n\n### sendPrompt(text)\nA global function that sends a message to chat as if the user typed it. Use it when the user's next step benefits from Claude thinking. Handle filtering, sorting, toggling, and calculations in JS instead.\n\n### Links\n`<a href=\"https://...\">` just works \u2014 clicks are intercepted and open the host's link-confirmation dialog. Or call `openLink(url)` directly.\n\n## When nothing fits\nPick the closest use case below and adapt. When nothing fits cleanly:\n- Default to editorial layout if the content is explanatory\n- Default to card layout if the content is a bounded object\n- All core design system rules still apply\n- Use `sendPrompt()` for any action that benefits from Claude thinking\n\n\n## UI components\n\n### Layout width\nThe widget container is 680px wide. Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr))` for responsive columns \u2014 auto-fit lets the grid pick column count by available width.\n\n### Aesthetic\nFlat, clean, white surfaces. Minimal 0.5px borders. Generous whitespace. No gradients, no shadows (except functional focus rings). Everything should feel native to claude.ai \u2014 like it belongs on the page, not embedded from somewhere else.\n\n### Tokens\n- Borders: always `0.5px solid var(--border)` (or `--border-strong` for emphasis)\n- Corner radius: `var(--radius)` for most elements, `12px` for cards\n- Cards: white bg (`var(--surface-2)`), 0.5px border, 12px radius, padding 1rem 1.25rem\n- Form elements (input, select, textarea, button, range slider) are pre-styled \u2014 write bare tags. Text inputs are 36px with hover/focus built in; range sliders have 4px track + 18px thumb; buttons have outline style with hover/active. Only add inline styles to override (e.g., different width).\n- Buttons: pre-styled with transparent bg, 0.5px `--border-strong` border, hover `--surface-1`, active scale(0.98). If it triggers sendPrompt, append a \u2197 arrow.\n- **Round every displayed number.** JS float math leaks artifacts \u2014 `0.1 + 0.2` gives `0.30000000000000004`, `7 * 1.1` gives `7.700000000000001`. Any number that reaches the screen (slider readouts, stat card values, axis labels, data-point labels, tooltips, computed totals) must go through `Math.round()`, `.toFixed(n)`, or `Intl.NumberFormat`. Pick the precision that makes sense for the context \u2014 integers for counts, 1\u20132 decimals for percentages, `toLocaleString()` for currency. For range sliders, also set `step=\"1\"` (or step=\"0.1\" etc.) so the input itself emits round values.\n- Spacing: use rem for vertical rhythm (1rem, 1.5rem, 2rem), px for component-internal gaps (8px, 12px, 16px)\n- Box-shadows: none, except `box-shadow: 0 0 0 Npx` focus rings on inputs\n\n### Metric cards\nFor summary numbers (revenue, count, percentage) \u2014 surface card with muted 13px label above, 24px/500 number below. `background: var(--surface-1)`, no border, `border-radius: var(--radius)`, padding 1rem. Use in grids of 2-4 with `gap: 12px`. Distinct from raised cards (which have white bg + border).\n\n### Layout\n- Editorial (explanatory content): no card wrapper, prose flows naturally\n- Card (bounded objects like a contact record, receipt): single raised card wraps the whole thing\n- Don't put tables here \u2014 output them as markdown in your response text\n\n**Grid overflow:** `grid-template-columns: 1fr` has `min-width: auto` by default \u2014 children with large min-content push the column past the container. Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` to clamp.\n\n**Table overflow:** Tables with many columns auto-expand past `width: 100%` if cell contents exceed it. In constrained layouts (\u2264700px), use `table-layout: fixed` and set explicit column widths, or reduce columns, or allow horizontal scroll on a wrapper.\n\n### Mockup presentation\nContained mockups \u2014 mobile screens, chat threads, single cards, modals, small UI components \u2014 should sit on a background surface (`var(--surface-1)` container with `border-radius: 12px` and padding, or a device frame) so they don't float naked on the widget canvas. Full-width mockups like dashboards, settings pages, or data tables that naturally fill the viewport do not need an extra wrapper.\n\n### 1. Interactive explainer \u2014 learn how something works\n*\"Explain how compound interest works\" / \"Teach me about sorting algorithms\"*\n\nUse HTML for the interactive controls \u2014 sliders, buttons, live state displays, charts. Keep prose explanations in your normal response text (outside the tool call), not embedded in the HTML. No card wrapper. Whitespace is the container.\n\n```html\n<div style=\"display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; margin: 0 0 1.5rem;\">\n  <label style=\"font-size: 14px; color: var(--text-secondary);\">Years</label>\n  <input type=\"range\" min=\"1\" max=\"40\" value=\"20\" id=\"years\" style=\"flex: 1;\" />\n  <span style=\"font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; min-width: 24px;\" id=\"years-out\">20</span>\n</div>\n\n<div style=\"display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; margin: 0 0 1.5rem;\">\n  <span style=\"font-size: 14px; color: var(--text-secondary);\">\u00a31,000 \u2192</span>\n  <span style=\"font-size: 24px; font-weight: 500;\" id=\"result\">\u00a33,870</span>\n</div>\n\n<div style=\"margin: 2rem 0; position: relative; height: 240px;\">\n  <canvas id=\"chart\"></canvas>\n</div>\n```\n\nUse `sendPrompt()` to let users ask follow-ups: `sendPrompt('What if I increase the rate to 10%?')`\n\n### 2. Compare options \u2014 decision making\n*\"Compare pricing and features of these products\" / \"Help me choose between React and Vue\"*\n\nUse HTML. Side-by-side card grid for options. Highlight differences with semantic colors. Interactive elements for filtering or weighting.\n\n- Each option in a card. Use badges for key differentiators. A leading Tabler icon (`<i class=\"ti ti-NAME\">` at 20px, `aria-hidden`) anchors each option visually \u2014 pick the most apt name per option.\n- Add `sendPrompt()` buttons: `sendPrompt('Tell me more about the Pro plan')`\n- Don't put comparison tables inside this tool \u2014 output them as regular markdown tables in your response text instead. The tool is for the visual card grid only.\n- When one option is recommended or \"most popular\", accent its card with `border: 2px solid var(--border-accent)` only (2px is deliberate \u2014 the only exception to the 0.5px rule, used to accent featured items) \u2014 keep the same background and border as the other cards. Add a small badge (e.g. \"Most popular\") above or inside the card header using `background: var(--bg-accent); color: var(--text-accent); font-size: 12px; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: var(--radius)`.\n\n### 3. Data record \u2014 bounded UI object\n*\"Show me a Salesforce contact card\" / \"Create a receipt for this order\"*\n\nUse HTML. Wrap the entire thing in a single raised card. All content is sans-serif since it's pure UI. Use an avatar/initials circle for people (see example below).\n\n```html\n<div style=\"background: var(--surface-2); border-radius: 12px; border: 0.5px solid var(--border); padding: 1rem 1.25rem;\">\n  <div style=\"display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; margin-bottom: 16px;\">\n    <div style=\"width: 44px; height: 44px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--bg-accent); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-weight: 500; font-size: 14px; color: var(--text-accent);\">MR</div>\n    <div>\n      <p style=\"font-weight: 500; font-size: 15px; margin: 0;\">Maya Rodriguez</p>\n      <p style=\"font-size: 13px; color: var(--text-secondary); margin: 0;\">VP of Engineering</p>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n  <div style=\"border-top: 0.5px solid var(--border); padding-top: 12px;\">\n    <table style=\"width: 100%; font-size: 13px;\">\n      <tr><td style=\"color: var(--text-secondary); padding: 4px 0;\"><i class=\"ti ti-mail\" style=\"font-size:16px; vertical-align:-2px; margin-right:6px\" aria-hidden=\"true\"></i>Email</td><td style=\"text-align: right; padding: 4px 0; color: var(--text-accent);\">m.rodriguez@acme.com</td></tr>\n      <tr><td style=\"color: var(--text-secondary); padding: 4px 0;\"><i class=\"ti ti-phone\" style=\"font-size:16px; vertical-align:-2px; margin-right:6px\" aria-hidden=\"true\"></i>Phone</td><td style=\"text-align: right; padding: 4px 0;\">+1 (415) 555-0172</td></tr>\n    </table>\n  </div>\n</div>\n```\n\n\n## Color palette\n\n9 color ramps, each with 7 stops from lightest to darkest. 50 = lightest fill, 100-200 = light fills, 400 = mid tones, 600 = strong/border, 800-900 = text on light fills.\n\n| Class | Ramp | 50 (lightest) | 100 | 200 | 400 | 600 | 800 | 900 (darkest) |\n|-------|------|------|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|------|\n| `c-purple` | Purple | #EEEDFE | #CECBF6 | #AFA9EC | #7F77DD | #534AB7 | #3C3489 | #26215C |\n| `c-teal` | Teal | #E1F5EE | #9FE1CB | #5DCAA5 | #1D9E75 | #0F6E56 | #085041 | #04342C |\n| `c-coral` | Coral | #FAECE7 | #F5C4B3 | #F0997B | #D85A30 | #993C1D | #712B13 | #4A1B0C |\n| `c-pink` | Pink | #FBEAF0 | #F4C0D1 | #ED93B1 | #D4537E | #993556 | #72243E | #4B1528 |\n| `c-gray` | Gray | #F1EFE8 | #D3D1C7 | #B4B2A9 | #888780 | #5F5E5A | #444441 | #2C2C2A |\n| `c-blue` | Blue | #E6F1FB | #B5D4F4 | #85B7EB | #378ADD | #185FA5 | #0C447C | #042C53 |\n| `c-green` | Green | #EAF3DE | #C0DD97 | #97C459 | #639922 | #3B6D11 | #27500A | #173404 |\n| `c-amber` | Amber | #FAEEDA | #FAC775 | #EF9F27 | #BA7517 | #854F0B | #633806 | #412402 |\n| `c-red` | Red | #FCEBEB | #F7C1C1 | #F09595 | #E24B4A | #A32D2D | #791F1F | #501313 |\n\n**How to assign colors**: Color should encode meaning, not sequence. Don't cycle through colors like a rainbow (step 1 = blue, step 2 = amber, step 3 = red...). Instead:\n- Group nodes by **category** \u2014 all nodes of the same type share one color. E.g. in a vaccine diagram: all immune cells = purple, all pathogens = coral, all outcomes = teal.\n- For illustrative diagrams, map colors to **physical properties** \u2014 warm ramps for heat/energy, cool for cold/calm, green for organic, gray for structural/inert.\n- Use **gray for neutral/structural** nodes (start, end, generic steps).\n- Use **2-3 colors per diagram**, not 6+. More colors = more visual noise. A diagram with gray + purple + teal is cleaner than one using every ramp.\n- **Prefer purple, teal, coral, pink** for general diagram categories. Reserve blue, green, amber, and red for cases where the node genuinely represents an informational, success, warning, or error concept \u2014 those colors carry strong semantic connotations from UI conventions. (Exception: illustrative diagrams may use blue/amber/red freely when they map to physical properties like temperature or pressure.)\n\n**Text on colored backgrounds:** Always use the 800 or 900 stop from the same ramp as the fill. Never use black, gray, or --text-primary on colored fills. **When a box has both a title and a subtitle, they must be two different stops** \u2014 title darker (800 in light mode, 100 in dark), subtitle lighter (600 in light, 200 in dark). Same stop for both reads flat; the weight difference alone isn't enough. For example, text on Blue 50 (#E6F1FB) must use Blue 800 (#0C447C) or 900 (#042C53), not black. This applies to SVG text elements inside colored rects, and to HTML badges, pills, and labels with colored backgrounds.\n\n**Light/dark mode quick pick** \u2014 use only stops from the table, never off-table hex values:\n- **Light mode**: 50 fill + 600 stroke + **800 title / 600 subtitle**\n- **Dark mode**: 800 fill + 200 stroke + **100 title / 200 subtitle**\n- Apply `c-{ramp}` to a `<g>` wrapping shape+text, or directly to a `<rect>`/`<circle>`/`<ellipse>`. Never to `<path>` \u2014 paths don't get ramp fill. For colored connector strokes use inline `stroke=\"#...\"` (any mid-ramp hex works in both modes). Dark mode is automatic for ramp classes. Available: c-gray, c-blue, c-red, c-amber, c-green, c-teal, c-purple, c-coral, c-pink.\n\nFor status/semantic meaning in UI (success, warning, danger) use CSS variables. For categorical coloring in both diagrams and UI, use these ramps.\n\n\n<!-- @generated by apps/cds-docs/scripts/gen-cds-skill.mjs from packages/cds/{CLAUDE.md,docs/**}. Do not edit by hand \u2014 edit the source docs and re-run `yarn workspace @ant/cds-docs gen:cds-skill`. -->\n\n# CDS tokens \u2014 vanilla\n\nThe Claude Design System token vocabulary for plain HTML/CSS/SVG\nsurfaces without React or Tailwind. Tokens are unprefixed CSS custom\nproperties (`--text-primary`, `--surface-1`, `--border`) declared on\n`:root` by `@ant/cds/tokens.vanilla.css`, with dark-mode overrides under\n`[data-mode=\"dark\"]` and `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`.\n\nReferences below to `CdsRoot`, `Button`, or Tailwind utilities belong to\nthe React build; in vanilla, read a utility like `bg-surface-1` as the\nunderlying `var(--surface-1)`.\n\n## Rules\n\n### Token rule\n\nReference purpose-layer tokens as CSS custom properties:\n\n```css\n/* GOOD */\nbackground: var(--surface-1);\ncolor: var(--text-secondary);\nborder: 0.5px solid var(--border);\n\n/* BAD \u2014 raw hex, invisible in dark mode */\ncolor: #3d3d3a;\n```\n\n| Property   | Tokens |\n| ---------- | ------ |\n| Background | `--surface-{0..3,popover,panel}` \u00b7 `--bg-{accent,danger,success,warning,pro,neutral}` \u00b7 `--fill-{role}` |\n| Text       | `--text-{primary,secondary,muted,disabled}` \u00b7 `--text-{accent,danger,success,warning,pro}` \u00b7 `--on-{role}` |\n| Border     | `--border` (default hairline) \u00b7 `--border-{strong,stronger}` \u00b7 `--border-{role}` |\n| Sizing     | `--h-control` \u00b7 `--pad-{sm,md,lg,xl}` \u00b7 `--gap-{xs,sm,md,lg,xl}` \u00b7 `--radius` |\n| Typography | `--font-{sans,mono,voice}` \u00b7 `--font-size-{caption,footnote,body,code,heading,title}` |\n| Shadow     | `--shadow-{sm,md,lg,popover}` |\n| Motion     | `--dur-{fast,snap,base,slow}` \u00b7 `--ease-{out,snap,overshoot}` |\n\n### Dark mode rule\n\nDark mode is `[data-mode=\"dark\"]` on `:root` (or `prefers-color-scheme: dark` with no explicit `data-mode`). All tokens flip automatically \u2014 never hardcode a dark-mode override.\n\n### Muted text rule\n\nSupporting copy uses `color: var(--text-secondary)`; reserve `var(--text-muted)` for placeholders, captions, and metadata. **Never** `opacity` on text \u2014 opacity multiplies against the background and drifts per-surface.\n\n### Accent rule\n\nAt most **one** accent-filled (`variant=\"primary\"`) Button per view; siblings use `secondary` or `ghost`. The `brand` (clay) role is reserved for Claude-initiated actions \u2014 send, generate \u2014 never ordinary user CTAs.\n\n### Restraint rule\n\nDefault to the quieter, lighter option \u2014 \"too cluttered\" is the most common design note.\n\n- `secondary` is the default Button; `primary` / `brand` read as aggressive \u2014 don't reach for them in popovers, banners, or dense tool/canvas surfaces.\n- Avoid disabled buttons. Keep them enabled and respond on use (disabled controls are low-contrast and show no tooltip on touch); use `disabledReason` only when you genuinely must disable.\n- Dense lists: bordered rows, not rounded-rect cards.\n\n### Elevation rule\n\n`surface-0` is the page canvas (via `--page-bg`); `1`/`2`/`3` step above it. At most **two** floating elevations (`panel` / `popover`) on screen at once. A third floating layer means `Dialog`, not popover-on-popover. Flat in-flow tiles (`rounded-card bg-surface-1 shadow-card-ring`) have no depth and don't count toward this limit.\n\n---\n\n## CDS principles\n\nHow something feels like Claude \u2014 the philosophy behind the tokens. Tokens tell you _what_ you can use; the [Rules](../CLAUDE.md#rules) tell you _how_ to apply them. These principles tell you _why_.\n\n## Claude-native\n\ncds is designed to be authored _by_ Claude as much as _for_ Claude's products. The `CLAUDE.md` you're reading is the system prompt; component docs are structured for retrieval; utilities are named so a model can guess them; the GenerateDemo page proves the loop works. A design system an LLM can use fluently is one humans can use fluently too.\n\n## Clay is Claude's color\n\n`brand` (clay) is reserved for what Claude does \u2014 send, generate, the spark mark. User-driven primary actions take the neutral `accent` blue; everything else stays gray. Holding clay back to a single role is what lets it carry meaning instead of becoming wallpaper.\n\n## Serif is Claude's voice\n\nClaude's responses render in serif; the surrounding chrome stays sans. Typography signals who's speaking before a word is read. cds ships `--font-voice` (the `font-voice` utility) for response surfaces.\n\n## Density adapts to the surface\n\nConsole, claude.ai and antfarm share the same components \u2014 `compact` for dev tools and power users, `comfortable` for consumer apps. Density is one switch on `CdsRoot`, not a per-component prop, so a product can change its feel without forking a single component.\n\n## Built to be extended\n\nEvery component takes `className`, every token is a public CSS var, and compound parts (`.Root`, `.Item`, `.Trigger`) sit under the porcelain helpers. The system expects you to compose past it \u2014 wrap, restyle, slot arbitrary children \u2014 not fork it.\n\n## Restraint over options\n\nOne accent per view, one elevation step, t-shirt sizes instead of 0\u201312 scales. Fewer decisions at the call site means fewer ways for two screens to drift apart \u2014 consistency comes from removing knobs, not policing them.\n\n## CDS tokens\n\nEvery visual decision in `@ant/cds` resolves to a `--*` CSS custom property. The TypeScript source of truth lives under `packages/cds/tokens/`; `yarn gen:tokens` emits the shipped CSS at [`src/generated/tokens.css`](../src/generated/tokens.css). Tokens are layered so that a single edit at the bottom (a hex value) propagates through ramps, roles, and purposes without touching component code.\n\n## The layer model\n\n```\n1. Base palette   --{hue}-{stop}      literal hex, mode-stable (gray, red, orange,\n                                          yellow, green, aqua, blue, violet, magenta)\n2. Theme ramps    --neutral-N         gray-N in light, gray-(900-N) in dark\n                  --alpha-N           neutral-900 @ fixed opacity (so it flips too)\n3. Elevation      --surface-{0..3}    0 = darkest, 3 = lightest, in BOTH modes\n4. Purpose        --surface-{popover, what components actually consume; includes the\n                   panel}, --text-*,  role mappings ({fill|bg|border|text}-{role})\n                   --fill-*, --on-*\n\u2014  page-bg        --page-bg           hook the host app sets to its canvas color\n5. Density        --h-control*,       px values; remapped by [data-density]\n                   --pad-*, --gap-*,\n                   --radius, --font-size-*,\n                   --leading-*\n6. Motion         --dur-*,            durations + easing curves (mode/density-invariant)\n                   --ease-*\n```\n\n**Components only read layer 4 (and 5 for sizing).** Layers 1\u20133 are wiring.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Base palette\n\nLiteral hex values, mode-stable \u2014 `gray-500` is the same pixel in light and dark. Nine hues share one 36-stop grid (0, 10\u2013100 by 10, 150\u2013800 by 50, 810\u2013900 by 10); every hue anchors 0 = `#ffffff` and 900 = `#0b0b0b`. Rarely referenced directly \u2014 reach for layers 2\u20134 and let them resolve here.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Theme ramps\n\n`--neutral-N` is `gray-N` in light and `gray-(900-N)` in dark, so `neutral-0` is always the near-background end and `neutral-900` the near-foreground end. Use it for \"contrast against the page\" (text, borders, fills); use `gray-*` when you mean a specific pixel value regardless of mode. `--alpha-N` is `neutral-900` at fixed opacity \u2014 a black wash in light, a white wash in dark, without per-mode overrides.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Elevation\n\n| Token             | Light     | Dark       | Use case     |\n| ----------------- | --------- | ---------- | ------------ |\n| `--surface-0` | `gray-20` | `gray-890` | Page         |\n| `--surface-1` | `gray-10` | `gray-830` | In-flow card |\n| `--surface-2` | `gray-0`  | `gray-750` | Panel        |\n| `--surface-3` | `gray-0`  | `gray-700` | Popover      |\n\nThe ordinal is absolute lightness in both modes: 0 is the darkest, 3 the lightest. `--surface-panel` and `--surface-popover` alias levels 2 and 3. The page canvas is the app's own choice \u2014 set `--page-bg` so knockout hairlines (focus ring inset, Pulse halo) blend into it; it defaults to `surface-0`.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Purpose\n\n**This is the layer components consume.**\n\n### Roles\n\nEach role maps a semantic meaning to a hue. Property-first pattern: `--fill-{role}` (solid hue-450), `--fill-{role}-hover` (hue-400), `--bg-{role}` (hue-100 / dark hue-800), `--border-{role}` (solid hue-250 in light / hue-700 in dark), `--text-{role}` (600 fg). Warning's fill diverges: yellow-200 / hover yellow-250. Brand uses named `clay-emphasized` / hover `clay` (not hue stops).\n\n| Role      | Hue    | Tokens                                                                                          |\n| --------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `accent`  | blue   | `--fill-accent{,-hover}`, `--bg-accent`, `--border-accent`, `--text-accent`     |\n| `brand`   | clay   | `--fill-brand{,-hover}`, `--on-brand` (fill-only \u2014 no text/bg/border)                   |\n| `danger`  | red    | `--fill-danger{,-hover}`, `--bg-danger`, `--border-danger`, `--text-danger`     |\n| `success` | green  | `--fill-success{,-hover}`, `--bg-success`, `--border-success`, `--text-success` |\n| `warning` | yellow | `--fill-warning{,-hover}`, `--bg-warning`, `--border-warning`, `--text-warning` |\n| `pro`     | purple | `--fill-pro{,-hover}`, `--bg-pro`, `--border-pro`, `--text-pro`                 |\n\n#### `git-*` roles\n\nDiff and PR/CR-state colors \u2014 `added`, `removed`, `modified`, `conflicting`, `merged`, `closed`, `draft`, plus `opened`/`queued` as aliases of `added`/`modified`. Each carries the full `text` / `fill{,-hover}` / `bg` / `border` / `on` suite. Values come from `@ant/epitaxy`'s `--extended-*` palette (not CDS ramp stops), so migrating claude.ai's diff UI onto these tokens is a rename; `fill` light is the Epitaxy hue darkened just enough for white `on-git-*` to pass AA.\n\n### Background vs. fill\n\nBoth are backgrounds; the split is saturation, and therefore which foreground token pairs on top.\n\n`bg-{role}` is the pale tint (hue-100 light / hue-800 dark) for passive status surfaces \u2014 Banner, Badge, chip. Light enough that `text-{role}` (hue-600) reads against it: a danger banner is `bg-danger` + `text-danger`. `fill-{role}` is the saturated solid (hue-450) for interactive controls \u2014 button, checkbox, toggle. Too dark for `text-{role}`, so it pairs with `on-{role}` (gray-0 / gray-900) instead; the 450 stop is chosen for WCAG contrast against `on-*`.\n\n|       | Background    | Foreground    | Example       |\n| ----- | ------------- | ------------- | ------------- |\n| Tint  | `bg-{role}`   | `text-{role}` | Banner, Badge |\n| Solid | `fill-{role}` | `on-{role}`   | Button        |\n\nThe token name encodes the pairing: use `bg-*` when the hue is ambient context behind body text; `fill-*` when the hue _is_ the control surface.\n\n### Purpose tokens\n\n| Token                        | Value (light)                                     | Use case                                         |\n| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |\n| `--text-primary`         | `neutral-900`                                     | Body text                                        |\n| `--text-secondary`       | `neutral-600`                                     | Supporting text                                  |\n| `--text-muted`           | `neutral-400`                                     | Placeholder, captions                            |\n| `--text-disabled`        | `alpha-4`                                         | Disabled labels                                  |\n| `--border`               | `alpha-2`                                         | Default 1px hairline                             |\n| `--border-strong`        | `alpha-3`                                         | Emphasized divider                               |\n| `--border-stronger`      | `neutral-900 / 40%`                               | Heavy divider                                    |\n| `--fill-primary`         | `neutral-900`                                     | Primary button bg                                |\n| `--fill-primary-hover`   | `neutral-750`                                     |                                                  |\n| `--fill-secondary`       | `hsl(0 0% 100% / 0.1)`                            | Secondary button bg                              |\n| `--fill-secondary-hover` | `alpha-1`                                         |                                                  |\n| `--fill-secondary-ring`  | `border` (light) / transparent (dark)             | Secondary button ring                            |\n| `--fill-field`           | `hsl(0 0% 100% / 0.5)` (light) / `alpha-1` (dark) | Field control bg (TextInput, TextArea, Combobox) |\n| `--fill-field-ring`      | `border` (light + dark)                           | Field control resting ring                       |\n| `--fill-ghost-hover`     | `alpha-1`                                         | Ghost button hover bg                            |\n| `--fill-control`         | `alpha-2`                                         | Avatar fallback bg                               |\n| `--fill-control-hover`   | `alpha-3`                                         |                                                  |\n| `--fill-disabled`        | `alpha-1`                                         | Disabled control bg                              |\n| `--on-primary`           | `neutral-0`                                       | Text on `fill-primary`                           |\n| `--on-accent`            | `gray-0`                                          | Text on `accent`                                 |\n| `--on-brand`             | `gray-0`                                          | Text on `brand`                                  |\n| `--on-danger`            | `gray-0`                                          | Text on `danger`                                 |\n| `--on-success`           | `gray-900`                                        | Text on `success`                                |\n| `--on-warning`           | `gray-900`                                        | Text on `warning`                                |\n| `--on-pro`               | `gray-0`                                          | Text on `pro`                                    |\n| `--focus-shadow`         | `0 0 0 1px accent, 0 0 6px 1px bg-accent`         | `focus-visible` ring                             |\n| `--shadow-sm`            | two-layer via `--shadow-color`                | Low elevation                                    |\n| `--shadow-md`            | two-layer via `--shadow-color`                | Card / panel                                     |\n| `--shadow-lg`            | two-layer via `--shadow-color`                | Dialog / sheet                                   |\n| `--shadow-popover`       | `0 8px 24px /12%, 0 2px 6px /8%`                  | Menu, dropdown popups                            |\n| `--surface-popover`      | `surface-3`                                       | Named alias                                      |\n| `--surface-panel`        | `surface-2`                                       | Named alias                                      |\n\n`--shadow-sm/md/lg` are two-layer composites (contact + diffused drop) driven by `--shadow-color`, which deepens to `black/24%` in dark mode (epitaxy parity). `--shadow-popover` is a fixed two-layer literal tuned for floating menus.\n\n---\n\n## CDS content\n\nHow to write the words that go inside cds components. Tokens decide how the UI _looks_; this decides how it _sounds_.\n\nThe voice is **intelligent, warm, unvarnished, and collaborative** \u2014 your smartest friend explaining something in plain terms. Friendly lives in the copy, not in extra chrome.\n\n## Mechanics\n\n- **Sentence case everywhere.** Buttons, headings, tabs, labels, menu items. \"Save changes\", not \"Save Changes\". Title Case is for proper nouns only (Claude, Opus, Anthropic Console).\n- **No terminal punctuation on labels and headings.** Helper text, descriptions, and empty-state body copy _do_ end with a period.\n- **Use contractions.** \"Can't\", \"you'll\", \"it's\". Conversational, not stiff.\n- **Active voice, verb first.** \"Delete project\", not \"Project deletion\".\n- **Ellipsis = in progress only.** \"Claude is thinking\u2026\". Not for trailing off, not for menu suffixes.\n- **No ampersands.** Spell out \"and\".\n- **Serial comma.** \"Chats, projects, and artifacts.\"\n\n## Pronouns\n\nUI speaks as the product, not as Claude and not as the user.\n\n| Context          | Use               | Example                                                 |\n| ---------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |\n| User's things    | **your**          | \"Your projects\" \u2014 never \"My projects\"                   |\n| Confirmations    | none / past tense | \"Saved\", \"Got it\" \u2014 never \"I saved it\"                  |\n| Errors           | **you / your**    | \"Your session expired\" \u2014 never \"I couldn't\u2026\"            |\n| Claude (in chat) | **I**             | Reserved for the chat surface; system UI never says \"I\" |\n\n## Words to avoid\n\n| Skip                                        | Why                                   | Instead          |\n| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------- |\n| \"successfully\"                              | The success toast _is_ the success    | \"File uploaded\"  |\n| \"please\"                                    | UI isn't asking a favor               | \"Enter a name\"   |\n| \"Click here\" / \"Tap to\u2026\"                    | Link text should name the destination | \"Read the docs\"  |\n| \"!\" on system copy                          | Reads as shouty                       | \"Settings saved\" |\n| \"leverage\", \"seamless\", \"unlock\", \"empower\" | Corporate filler                      | Say what it does |\n| \"simply\", \"just\", \"easy\"                    | Presumes \u2014 and condescends            | Cut it           |\n\n## Patterns\n\n**Buttons / CTAs** \u2014 verb first, 1\u20133 words, sentence case, no punctuation. \"Create project\", \"Upgrade to Pro\". Not \"OK\", \"Submit\", or \"Click to continue\".\n\n**Errors** \u2014 say what happened, then what to do. One sentence, no \"Error:\" prefix, no first person. \"That name's already taken. Try another.\" Never surface raw exception strings.\n\n**Empty states** \u2014 an invitation, not an apology. Headline names the space (\"Start your first project\"), one-line body explains it, CTA is a verb (\"Create project\"). Skip \"Nothing here yet.\"\n\n**Placeholders** \u2014 a real example of valid input (\"name@company.com\", \"Summarize this document\"). No \"e.g.\" prefix, don't repeat the field label.\n\n**Links** \u2014 describe where they go (\"Learn more\", \"View pricing\"). Keep them at the end of the sentence; punctuation sits outside the link.\n\n## Do / Don't\n\n| Do                                 | Don't                                  |\n| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |\n| \"File uploaded\"                    | \"Your file was uploaded successfully!\" |\n| \"Enter a workspace name\"           | \"Please enter a workspace name.\"       |\n| \"Couldn't connect to Slack. Retry\" | \"Error: I was unable to connect.\"      |\n| \"Your projects\"                    | \"My projects\"                          |\n| \"Create project\"                   | \"Click Here To Get Started\"            |\n| \"Connect Slack\"                    | \"Add the Slack Connector\"              |\n\n\nDo not overthink. Try to keep thinking below 500 tokens. If the visual is complex and requires more reasoning effort, consider creating an artifact instead.",
                                "uuid": "ea7ca105-cc85-4c51-b47d-a51cb9995dc7"
                            }
                        ],

                        "text": "Here are 4 distinct UI concepts for your admin dashboard \u2014 pick the one that feels right and we'll lock it in before writing the prompt.",

                "uuid": "019fb8f9-948d-7d8a-9bd3-2e41beb37c2c",
                "text": "Based on everything we've discussed, here are your custom instructions for the **Custom Instructions tab** in AI Studio:\n\n---\n\n```\n## PROJECT OVERVIEW\nYou are building a private WebRTC-based KYC Verification Platform prototype. This is a real, functional application \u2014 not a demo or mockup. Every feature must work end to end.\n\n## TECH STACK \u2014 NEVER DEVIATE\n- Framework: Next.js 14 with App Router only\n- Styling: Tailwind CSS only \u2014 no other CSS frameworks\n- Real-time: Socket.io for WebRTC signaling and chat\n- Video/Audio: WebRTC with RTCPeerConnection (browser native)\n- Location: Browser Geolocation API + Leaflet.js map\n- Database: MongoDB Atlas with Mongoose ODM\n- Video Storage: MongoDB GridFS (for offline recorded messages only)\n- Auth: JWT stored in localStorage (prototype only)\n- TURN/STUN: Metered.ca credentials (provided in env)\n\n## ICE SERVER CONFIGURATION \u2014 USE EXACTLY AS PROVIDED\nAlways use this exact WebRTC ICE config from environment variables:\n- NEXT_PUBLIC_STUN_URL\n- NEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_URL\n- NEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_URL_TCP\n- NEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_URL_443\n- NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNS_URL\n- NEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_USERNAME\n- NEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_CREDENTIAL\nNever hardcode ICE credentials in any file.\n\n## UI DESIGN \u2014 NON NEGOTIABLE\n- Theme: Light, bright, white \u2014 NOT dark theme under any circumstance\n- Style: Minimal, professional, generous white space (not empty space \u2014 content should breathe)\n- Dashboard type: Light sidebar navigation with metric stat cards and live session grid\n- Font: Clean sans-serif system font\n- Colors: Subtle accent colors only \u2014 never loud or saturated backgrounds\n- Borders: Hairline borders (0.5\u20131px), soft border-radius on cards (10\u201312px)\n- No gradients, no heavy shadows, no decorative elements\n- Every state must have UI feedback: connecting, waiting, streaming, approved, rejected, disconnected\n\n## APPLICATION SCREENS\n\n### User Side (no auth required)\n1. Consent screen (homepage /):\n   - Prototype mode: camera + mic + location permissions requested immediately on load\n   - Two sections explaining KYC: plain English + legal terms\n   - One \"I Agree & Continue\" button that starts the WebRTC stream\n2. KYC session screen (same page after consent):\n   - Shows \"Waiting for admin review...\" status\n   - Shows attempt count (e.g. \"Attempt 1 of 5\")\n   - If admin offline for 120 seconds: offer to record a video message (no time limit but compress before storing in GridFS)\n   - If rejected: show rejection message + remaining attempts\n   - If approved: transition to chat screen\n\n### Admin Side (JWT auth required)\n1. Login page (/admin/login):\n   - Hardcoded credentials: username: admin, password: admin123\n   - JWT issued on login, stored in localStorage\n   - Redirect to dashboard on success\n2. Dashboard (/admin):\n   - Stat cards: active streams, approved today, rejected today, awaiting review\n   - Live session grid (3 columns): each card shows mini feed + LIVE tag + mic status + session ID + wait time + approve/reject icons\n   - Click any session card \u2192 opens full screen session view\n3. Full screen session view (/admin/session/[id]):\n   - Left: live video feed (full height)\n   - Right top: location map (Leaflet, collapsed pill \u2192 click to expand)\n   - Right bottom: chat window (post-approval only)\n   - Controls: switch camera (front/back via socket), toggle mic (default OFF), resync feed (ICE restart via socket), approve button, reject button\n   - Post-approval controls: save chat, save location, capture snapshot for KYC log, reject and terminate\n   - Close session: admin writes closing note \u2192 user sees goodbye message\n   - Terminate session: fixed system message + optional admin note \u2192 user sees termination screen\n4. Recorded messages (/admin/recorded):\n   - List/grid of offline video recordings\n   - Each card: session ID, timestamp, duration, status (unreviewed/reviewed), play button, delete option\n   - Badge on dashboard showing unreviewed count\n\n## CORE FEATURES & LOGIC\n\n### WebRTC\n- Peer connection uses ICE servers from environment variables only\n- ICE restart (not full reconnect) on resync\n- Camera switch fires socket event to user device to switch getUserMedia constraints\n- Mic toggle controlled on admin side (mute/unmute remote audio track)\n- On user disconnect: admin sees \"User disconnected\" on session card\n- On admin disconnect: user sees \"Admin disconnected\" message\n\n### Session & Attempt Tracking (MongoDB)\n- Each session stored in MongoDB with: sessionId, startTime, status, attemptNumber, locationData, snapshotUrl\n- Max 5 attempts per user IP per hour\n- Attempt count and timestamps persisted in MongoDB \u2014 never in memory only\n- After 5 rejections in 1 hour: user sees cooldown message with time remaining\n\n### Admin Offline Flow\n- Socket.io tracks admin online/offline status\n- On user connect: check if admin is online\n- If admin offline: start 120 second countdown on user screen (subtle, not alarming)\n- If admin comes online within 120s: countdown disappears, session starts normally\n- If 120s expires: offer video recording Create the following folder structure:\n\n/app\n  /admin\n    /login\n      page.tsx\n    /session\n      /[id]\n        page.tsx\n    /recorded\n      page.tsx\n    page.tsx\n  /api\n    /auth\n      route.ts\n    /sessions\n      route.ts\n    /socket\n      route.ts\n  page.tsx (user consent + KYC screen)\n/lib\n  /db.ts (MongoDB Atlas connection via Mongoose)\n  /jwt.ts (JWT issue + verify helpers)\n  /socket.ts (Socket.io server instance)\n/models\n  /Session.ts (Mongoose schema)\n/public\n/server.ts (custom Next.js server with Socket.io attached)\n\nCreate .env.local with these placeholder keys:\nMONGODB_URI=\nJWT_SECRET=\nNEXT_PUBLIC_STUN_URL=\nNEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_URL=\nNEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_URL_TCP=\nNEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_URL_443=\nNEXT_PUBLIC_TURNS_URL=\nNEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_USERNAME=\nNEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_CREDENTIAL=\nVAPID_PUBLIC_KEY=\nVAPID_PRIVATE_KEY=\n\nAlso create package.json with all required dependencies: next, react, react-dom, typescript, tailwindcss, socket.io, socket.io-client, mongoose, jsonwebtoken, leaflet, react-leaflet, web-push, @types/leaflet, @types/jsonwebtoken, @types/web-push.\n\nCreate tailwind.config.ts and tsconfig.json with strict mode enabled.\n\nDo not build any UI yet. Foundation only.\n```\n\n---\n\n### \ud83d\uddc4\ufe0f PROMPT 1 \u2014 MongoDB Session Schema\n```\nCreate the Mongoose Session schema at /models/Session.ts with these fields:\n\n- sessionId: String, required, unique (generate with crypto.randomUUID())\n- ipAddress: String, required (for attempt tracking)\n- attemptNumber: Number, required, default 1\n- startTime: Date, required, default Date.now\n- endTime: Date\n- status: String, enum: ['waiting', 'active', 'approved', 'rejected', 'terminated', 'recorded'], default 'waiting'\n- locationData: { latitude: Number, longitude: Number, accuracy: Number }\n- snapshotUrl: String (base64 compressed image, stored on approval capture)\n- chatLog: Array of { sender: String (admin/user), message: String, fileUrl: String, timestamp: Date }\n- recordingGridFSId: String (GridFS file ID for offline recorded video)\n- recordingDuration: Number (seconds)\n- adminNote: String (closing or termination note from admin)\n- rejectionCount: Number, default 0\n- cooldownUntil: Date (set when rejectionCount hits 5)\n\nAlso create /lib/db.ts that connects to MongoDB Atlas using MONGODB_URI from .env.local. Use a cached connection pattern so it doesn't reconnect on every request in Next.js.\n\nAlso create /lib/jwt.ts with two functions:\n- signToken(payload): signs a JWT with JWT_SECRET, expires in 8 hours\n- verifyToken(token): verifies and returns payload, throws on invalid\n```\n\n---\n\n### \u26a1 PROMPT 2 \u2014 Custom Server + Socket.io\n```\nCreate server.ts at the project root \u2014 a custom Next.js server that attaches Socket.io.\n\nSocket.io events to implement:\n\nCLIENT EVENTS (received by server):\n- 'admin:join' \u2192 mark admin as online, emit 'admin:status' to all users with { online: true }\n- 'admin:leave' \u2192 mark admin as offline, emit 'admin:status' to all with { online: false }\n- 'user:join' \u2192 user connects with sessionId, notify admin with 'session:new' { sessionId, startTime }\n- 'user:leave' \u2192 user disconnects, emit 'session:ended' { sessionId } to admin\n- 'webrtc:offer' \u2192 relay offer from user to admin { sessionId, offer }\n- 'webrtc:answer' \u2192 relay answer from admin to user { sessionId, answer }\n- 'webrtc:ice-candidate' \u2192 relay ICE candidates between peers { sessionId, candidate, from }\n- 'admin:camera-switch' \u2192 relay to specific user { sessionId, facingMode }\n- 'admin:resync' \u2192 relay to specific user { sessionId } \u2014 triggers ICE restart on user side\n- 'session:approve' \u2192 relay to specific user { sessionId }, update session status in MongoDB\n- 'session:reject' \u2192 relay to specific user { sessionId, rejectionCount, attemptsLeft }, update MongoDB\n- 'session:terminate' \u2192 relay to specific user { sessionId, message, adminNote }\n- 'session:close' \u2192 relay to specific user { sessionId, adminNote }\n- 'chat:message' \u2192 relay chat message to correct peer { sessionId, sender, message, fileUrl, timestamp }\n- 'location:update' \u2192 relay user GPS to admin { sessionId, latitude, longitude, accuracy }\n- 'recording:save' \u2192 receive base64 video chunk from user, save to MongoDB GridFS\n\nSERVER EVENTS (emitted by server):\n- 'admin:status' { online: boolean }\n- 'session:new' { sessionId, startTime }\n- 'session:ended' { sessionId }\n- 'webrtc:offer', 'webrtc:answer', 'webrtc:ice-candidate' (relayed)\n- 'session:approved', 'session:rejected', 'session:terminated', 'session:closed'\n- 'chat:message' (relayed)\n- 'location:update' (relayed)\n\nTrack admin socket ID in memory. Track user sessions in a Map of sessionId \u2192 socketId.\nUpdate package.json start script to run server.ts via ts-node.\n```\n\n---\n\n### \ud83d\udd10 PROMPT 3 \u2014 Admin Auth API + Login Page\n```\nBuild two things:\n\n1. Check next.config.ts \u2014 make sure it does NOT have \n   any pages router config, custom document references, \n   or experimental flags that conflict with App Router\n3. Check package.json \u2014 make sure there is no \"hono\" \n   package installed. If it exists remove it immediately \n   as it conflicts with Next.js App Router\n4. Do NOT run npm run build at all \u2014 AI Studio uses \n   dev server for preview, build is not needed here\n\nReport what you find at each step.\n```\n\n---\n\nThe key insight is that **AI Studio runs in dev mode** \u2014 you don't need `npm run build` to work.                 "uuid": "019fbc74-c2a6-759c-91ee-64a2b7625e3f",
                "text": "I have completed the full security and quality audit across the project. The development server has been successfully restarted (npm run dev) and is running cleanly without errors. As instructed, npm run build was not executed.\nHere is a comprehensive report of what was found and fixed:\n1. API Security\n\n* Found: POST /api/sessions had JWT validation, which blocked unauthenticated users from initiating the KYC stream. /api/push lacked any form of protection, making it vulnerable to public spamming.\n* Fixed: Removed JWT validation specifically from POST /api/sessions to support the unauthenticated user flow. Secured /api/push by adding strict JWT validation for registering subscriptions and implementing an internal secret header (X-Internal-Secret) for the user-waiting trigger to ensure it can only be invoked by the backend securely. Updated the admin dashboard to pass the JWT bearer token when saving subscriptions.\n\n2. Environment Variables & WebRTC Security\n\n* Found: WebRTC ICE server credentials (NEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_USERNAME, NEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_CREDENTIAL, etc.) were directly referenced in client-side code (page.tsx and SessionClient.tsx), inadvertently exposing them directly in the bundle.\n* Fixed: Created a dedicated /api/ice-servers endpoint to securely aggregate and deliver ICE configurations on demand. Refactored initWebRTC in both the user client and admin client to fetch these credentials dynamically, fully removing direct exposure of TURN configurations from the client-side source code.\n\n3. Socket.io Security\n\n* Found: Admin-only socket events lacked strict authorization checks. A malicious user could emit admin:join to impersonate an admin, or manually emit session:approve, session:reject, and admin:resync to hijack the workflow.\n* Fixed: Enforced JWT verification directly inside the admin:join socket listener to securely validate the admin identity before assigning adminSocketId. Added strict authorization guards (if (socket.id !== adminSocketId) return;) to all privileged administrative socket events, completely preventing users from emitting admin actions or injecting webrtc:answer payloads as the admin.\n\n4. MongoDB Data Integrity\n\n* Found: The Session model lacked basic validation (bounds, lengths, enums). Furthermore, update operations in server.ts and route.ts bypassed schema validation, and raw sessionId payload fields were used directly in lookup queries, exposing potential NoSQL injection vectors.\n* Fixed: Hardened the Mongoose SessionSchema with strict enum types, maxlength, min, and max constraints. Patched all findOneAndUpdate and updateOne database queries to include { runValidators: true }. Added explicit string typecasting (String(sessionId)) across all query filters to sanitize user inputs.\n\n5. General Quality\n\n* Found: Several async utility functions and socket listeners (e.g., switchCamera, webrtc:answer, webrtc:ice-candidate) lacked try/catch boundaries.\n* Fixed: Added comprehensive try/catch error handling to all asynchronous socket listeners and MediaStream functions to prevent unhandled promise rejections. Audited all console.log statements to ensure no sensitive parameters were exposed, and verified the codebase is clean of any remaining TODO or placeholder comments.\n\nCurrent State:\nThe dev server is operational. The User Consent page (/), Admin Login (/admin/login), Admin Dashboard (/admin), and Live Session interface (/admin/session/[id]) are fully active, secure, and functioning as intended.",

                            "code": "\nimport zipfile, subprocess, os\n\ndef extract_pdf_ocr(path, prefix):\n    z = zipfile.ZipFile(path)\n    names = z.namelist()\n    manifest = z.read('manifest.json').decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')\n    import json\n    m = json.loads(manifest)\n    n = m['num_pages']\n    texts = []\n    for i in range(1, n+1):\n        img_data = z.read(f'{i}.jpeg')\n        imgpath = f'/tmp/{prefix}_{i}.jpeg'\n        with open(imgpath, 'wb') as f:\n            f.write(img_data)\n        r = subprocess.run(['tesseract', imgpath, 'stdout'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)\n        texts.append(r.stdout)\n    return texts\n\nfiles_map = {\n    'Aadarsh_card_Pancard.pdf': 'pan',\n    'Trust_registration_form_1.pdf': 'regform',\n    'AAZTS5070P_Affidavit_draft_1.pdf': 'affidavit',\n}\nresults = {}\nfor fname, prefix in files_map.items():\n    path = os.path.join('/mnt/project', fname)\n    results[fname] = extract_pdf_ocr(path, prefix)\n    print(fname, \"pages:\", len(results[fname]))\n"

                "uuid": "019fc7a9-ffbe-709e-81a8-019f40850854",
                "text": "Good question, and yeah, let's clear up something first. FCRA is specifically about receiving foreign donations into India, it does not stop you from sending money out, like if you're importing wheelchairs or paying an international vendor. That falls under normal RBI slash FEMA rules for outward remittance, which any regular current account can handle, so you're fine there even without FCRA for now.\n\nFor the bank itself, I'd lean towards HDFC or ICICI for your day to day trust account. Both have dedicated NGO or trust banking desks, handle multiple trustee signatories smoothly, have solid net banking that actually works without the runaround you just had, and can process international outward payments without much friction. And yes, you can absolutely have multiple bank accounts for a charitable trust, that is completely legal, as long as all accounts are properly recorded in your trust's books and the trustees have passed a resolution authorizing each one. Keep in mind though, once you do get your FCRA certification in a few years, that specific account has to be opened at the State Bank of India's main branch in Delhi, that part is non negotiable by law.",
